summary: Biography of Texas senator Ted Cruz, from his teenage schooling in libertarian free-market ideology through Princeton and his Senate career, covering the 2013 shutdown, hardline positions and dirty campaign tactics up to his 2018 race.

evidence.note: story opens in Cleveland in 1939 with Fred Clark founding a free-market foundation
Roland Story founds his Houston free-enterprise institute in 1976 and recruits teens
Cruz born 1970 in Calgary to a Cuban father, family moves to Texas in 1974
teen corroborators memorise the Constitution and tour Texas clubs as ideological training
Harvard Law, Texas solicitor general 2003 to 2008, Supreme Court cases
Senate fights over abortion access and the 2013 shutdown over Obamacare
anti-Muslim and anti-refugee proposals, ties to a violent anti-abortion activist
father Rafael Cruz: inflammatory claims and disputed Cuban revolutionary past
2018 Senate race against O'Rourke and deceptive campaign texts and mailers

notes: Transcript renders the Princeton roommate as Craig Mason; the Hangover writer is Craig Mazin. Covered span starts in 1939 because Fred Clark's foundation and Roland Story's program get a long segment as the ideological roots of Cruz. Rafael Cruz's Cuban past is a short segment, so CU is left out of setting. Description frames this as the first of two 2018 midterm episodes, but the content is a full biography, so deep-dive.
